items.from: UK Government (Department for Business, Energy & Industrial Strategy) and ARIA
items.capacity: Chairman of ARIA (non-executive chair; founding chair)
items.fact: The GOV.UK press release of 19 July 2022 announced Matt Clifford MBE as ARIA Chairman, taking up the post on 15 August 2022. He said on 7 September 2026 that he had completed his first full term, and the Register reported the Secretary of State asked him to remain until 6 November 2026; no reappointment was found.
items.quote: as he takes post on 15 August, acting as the steward for ARIA's effective governance
items.missing: ARIA's own dated leadership or appointment page (the undated ARIA leadership page was seen only in a search summary); the term length and any reappointment terms; an ARIA or GOV.UK record of the actual handover on or after 6 November 2026.
items.notes: Times Higher Education (read, 7 September 2026) says Clifford has been the agency's founding chair since its inception in 2022. A saxbam.com copy of the 2022 announcement returned HTTP 404 when read. Clifford's 7 September 2026 post is quoted in TNW (read).

items.capacity: Commercial licence (purpose, scope and value not stated in the reporting read)
items.fact: page not read: the Sifted report of 7 September 2026 (Freya Pratty) was not readable past its lede in my reader. The Next Web, which I read, relays Sifted that ARIA holds a commercial licence with Anthropic, alongside other AI providers; no purpose, value or other provider is named in what I read.
items.quote: ARIA holds a commercial licence with Anthropic, alongside other AI providers.
items.missing: Full Sifted text; the licence's purpose, scope, value, term and start date; the names of the other AI providers; any ARIA or Anthropic primary record of the licence.
items.notes: Sifted URL: https://sifted.eu/articles/matt-clifford-quits-aria/ (byline Freya Pratty, dated September 7, 2026 in the page header). A search for an ARIA-Anthropic licence (query 11) returned only unrelated US and California Claude deals, so this rests on one reported claim.

items.to: Teams funded under the Safeguarded AI programme (for example Hashberg Ltd)
items.capacity: Safeguarded AI programme, Mathematics for Safe AI opportunity space, backed by 59 million pounds
items.fact: The ARIA Safeguarded AI programme is backed by 59 million pounds and aims to use fleets of AI agents to model and verify critical cyber and cyber-physical systems. The funded-projects page lists teams such as Hashberg Ltd with no amounts shown, and I found no named frontier AI company (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind) as a recipient or partner on the ARIA pages read.
items.quote: Backed by £59m, Safeguarded AI sits within the Trust Everything, Everywhere opportunity space
items.missing: Per-team amounts for the funded projects; an ARIA list of every programme that funds frontier AI work beyond Safeguarded AI; confirmation of any AI company holding a funded or partner role with ARIA.
items.notes: A grant-aggregator listing (grantedai.com, not read) describes a 10 million dollar joint call with Google DeepMind, Schmidt Sciences, the Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA and Google.org for multi-agent AI safety research; it is unverified and not an ARIA record. A third-party wiki's claim that a 18m Phase 2 award was dropped in November 2025 is also unverified. The funded-projects page footer names the sponsoring department as the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade.

items.capacity: Managing Director, International Affairs (engagement with governments outside North America)
items.fact: Clifford joined Anthropic about 2 September 2026 (TNW says five days before his 7 September resignation) and at first kept the ARIA chair. An ARIA spokesperson said the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade had formally reviewed the arrangement and that robust mitigations were agreed with it, including Clifford stepping back from any ARIA business where a conflict could arise; Anthropic said he had no involvement in or visibility of ARIA's commercial discussions with the company.
items.publisher: The Next Web (relaying Sifted; ARIA spokesperson and Anthropic statements as reported)
items.quote: Robust mitigations had been agreed with the department
items.missing: The department's own published statement and its written assessment of the conflict (the Commons committee asked for these); the date of the review; the full list of mitigations beyond stepping back from ARIA business.
items.notes: The ARIA spokesperson's and Anthropic's statements are as reported by Sifted and relayed by TNW; the Sifted body was not readable. The ARIA footer (aria.org.uk funded-projects page, read) names the sponsoring department as the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade. A search summary of the Guardian's reporting (not read) says Anthropic stated the arrangement was agreed with ARIA and the department that appoints the chair.

items.from: Dame Chi Onwurah MP, chair of the House of Commons Science, Innovation and Technology Committee
items.to: ARIA governance and the UK government
items.fact: Onwurah called Clifford's dual role a 'clear conflict of interest' in the week before 7 September 2026, as reported by Times Higher Education and The Register, and Renascence (dated 3 September 2026) carries the same description. On 7 September she said 'important questions remain' and that she had written to the government seeking clarity; TNW reports the Guardian's account that he was forced to stand down under pressure from senior MPs, and the Guardian article itself was not read.
items.missing: The Guardian article itself; the committee's own 7 September statement and the text of Onwurah's letter to government (both described in search summaries only); any ministerial reply.
items.notes: Clifford's own 7 September statement (self_report, quoted in TNW and THE): 'I have decided to step down to ensure my new role at Anthropic doesn't become a distraction'. Renascence (read, 3 September 2026) relays The Register's 'clear conflict of interest'. Search summaries (not read) put the letter at 4 September 2026.

items.from: Secretary of State (department not named in the reporting read)
items.fact: No successor or interim chair was found in any result read. The Register reported on 7 September 2026 that the Secretary of State asked Clifford to remain until 6 November 2026 while a new chair was appointed.
items.quote: asked him to remain until November 6 while a new chair is appointed
items.missing: An official appointment notice (GOV.UK or ARIA) for a successor or interim chair dated on or after 6 November 2026; the date the post was filled; confirmation of Clifford's actual departure date.
items.notes: Two successor searches (queries 3 and 9) returned mostly Australian ARIA (music industry body) results. An undated parliamentary-question snippet (not read) refers to recruitment for ARIA's first Chair and CEO, which is probably from 2022 and not about the 2026 vacancy. Today is 12 November 2026, so the 6 November date has passed.

items.capacity: Non-Executive Chair, ARIA (register entry); declared interest: Director, Entrepreneur First
items.fact: page not read: the ARIA register of interests PDF for board members and programme directors (September 2023) was found, but my reader returned it as a binary PDF and I could not open it. Per a search summary (not read), it lists Clifford as Non-Executive Chair with one declared interest, Director of Entrepreneur First, and says the register would be updated quarterly; no later version was found.
items.missing: The PDF's contents (open it with a PDF reader); any ARIA register update after September 2023; the current register on aria.org.uk; whether the Anthropic role was declared.
items.notes: Also found in search, not read: the ARIA conflict of interests policy PDF (https://aria.org.uk/media/qnmf1dsu/aria-conflict-of-interests-policy.pdf) and a GOV.UK page of Clifford's declared outside interests as a ministerial appointee, updated 24 February 2025 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/matt-cliffords-declared-outside-interests/matt-cliffords-declared-outside-interests), which covers his government role rather than ARIA.
